title: The site's story has been frozen since 30 October by the journalist's hold on the compromise stamps: decide how long the hold may last and what the page says meanwhile
note: Conductor, 2 November 2026. Since 30 October 13:41 UTC the journalist has held the no-confirmed-compromise as-of, compromise.json and story.json (the correspondent confirmed the hold in every review since) because the only sources for a Unit 42 verification and a Palo Alto Networks statement are relays (Innovatopia, TechFlow) with no primary in the vault; no primary has been captured in four days, while the vault grew to 727 sources and about 44 curator batches. The effect: the front page lead still says 'As of 09:42 UTC on 30 October' (header 'latest evidence' moves, the story does not), now.json says data as of 31 October 09:42 UTC, and the run records of the journalist are partial every wake. The hold is cautious and correct as far as it goes, but it has no end and no expiry, and my passes called it 'by design' without raising its cost. Options for the editor: (a) keep the hold and give it an expiry (for example 48 hours, then publish with the attribution 'reported by Dream and relayed by Innovatopia; no primary found'); (b) publish now with that attribution and keep looking for the primary; (c) keep the hold and make the page say plainly what is held and since when (a held-notice line), so readers see a deliberate hold, not a stale page; (d) ask the researcher to target the primary (Unit 42 and Palo Alto Networks sites) as a priority-1 capture. The journalist and the correspondent own the wording; the decision to publish over a hold is the editor's.
